summary: r156b (gate round 1): A RECORD OF THE MODES, NOT A RULE ABOUT TIMESTAMPS. r156 inferred a permission change from timestamps ('ctime passed the stamp, mtime did not'). That heuristic had three defects — the gate found one; the second is worse and the gate could not see it from macOS: (1) the gate's P2 — blind after any touch or write in the same call; (2) on Linux `chmod` moves a file's ctime EVEN WHEN THE MODE IS UNCHANGED (verified on the Linux box, kernel 6.12: a no-op chmod moved every file's ctime) — so `chmod -R` over a tree that already has the mode would have reported the WHOLE TREE as 'cannot hold'; on macOS a no-op chmod moves nothing, so the same code flooded on one platform and not the other; (3) it reported a file rewritten with identical content and a preserved mtime (cp -p over an existing file). The child now lists 'mode:uid:gid<TAB>path' for the files the snapshot holds (git's own list; .tmax contents excluded like the snapshot's pathspec) BEFORE and AFTER the command; a path whose line differs is reported unless the tree diff already covers it. `touch` cannot move it, a chmod that changes nothing cannot appear in it, it holds after a write, and it sees ownership changes. Since a permission or ownership change always moves the ctime, the after-listing is skipped when the stamp scan found nothing — a call that wrote no file pays ONE listing. Also from round 1: the scan takes exactly 400 entries per pass (it admitted a 401st since r155c), and the report's order no longer depends on the second pass having found anything. Found by the full suite while verifying, fixed here: the listing is line-based, so a name CONTAINING a newline arrived in pieces and was reported — the report now names only paths that exist on disk (the r155 round-4 'newline name' test caught it). The symlink scan from r156 stays.

title: the examination cap counts CANDIDATES, not held entries - and a hit is no longer silent
detail: The r158 gate's round-2 reproduced DECLARED limit: the report examined only the first 400 entries of a class and HELD entries counted against the bound. One ordinary call that touched 401 held files, edited a tracked file and wrote inside a nested repository showed the row '[ckpt main/1-a2 ✓]' with no error row - an unqualified success for a command whose nested write the checkpoint cannot hold.

1) Membership is a hash lookup (fikra-ollama-list-hash + hashmap-get), replacing three O(entries x held) member scans per entry - the reason the cap was 400. The three classes (scan entries, mode/owner entries, ignored entries) are each examined in their own pass with a shared seen-set (a path two listings name is reported once). The cap is fikra-ollama-examine-cap = 4000 per class and counts examined entries of that class.

2) A cap hit reports: 'the change scan examined only its first 4000 entries - coverage beyond it is not established' (joined with the 60 KB clause when both apply), and the checkpoint-error carries a 'qual' field the replay routes to that action's row: '[ckpt <ref> - coverage not established]' when nothing was named, '[ckpt <ref> - not held]' when a path is. Events without qual (older logs, other emitters) read 'not held'. '0 path(s) ... not revertable' is no longer said in the status line for a cap-only report.

3) THE PER-PASS SETS ARE NOT UNIFORM, on purpose (r156): the mode/owner pass and the ignored pass exclude by the tree diff only - a path the trees HOLD can carry a change they cannot record. My first r159 cut gave all three passes the same sets and every permission report went silent: the full suite returned 13 failures (the r156 family + two downstream). Fixed, and pinned at unit level (MODE-ROW): with the bug re-introduced the pin fails on '[ckpt main/9-a6 ✓]'.

4) Test hygiene: the r158b crowd test and the new crowd test carry a 90 s budget (the suite's uniform 20 s timed out in both r158 gate full runs); the r157 console.log-only debug block is removed in its own commit (40d0df74).
